# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (May 26, 2026)

## OVERVIEW
Today's development focused on enhancing `op-conductor-ops` with a new cluster bootstrapping command, fixing Docker image build issues, and improving CI workflows for Docker image publishing.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Enhanced Operational Tooling
A new `bootstrap-standby-cluster` command was added to `op-conductor-ops` to facilitate the creation of fresh Raft clusters for conductor/sequencer pairs, leaving conductors paused and sequencers unstarted for controlled deployment scenarios ([#634](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/634)).

### Docker Image Hardening and Build Fixes
Several Docker images, including `proxyd` and `replica-healthcheck`, were updated to use hardened Chainguard base images for improved security. Additionally, a fix was implemented to ignore lifecycle scripts during dependency installation in Dockerfiles for `replica-healthcheck`, preventing potential build issues ([#625](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/625), [#632](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/632)).

### CI/CD Workflow Improvements
The CI pipeline was updated to correctly forward plan matrix tags to the Docker publishing process, ensuring that release publishes use proper semver tags instead of sanitized GitHub reference names ([#633](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/633)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were reported today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Nondeterministic Semver Lock Generation
Issue [#21032](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21032) reports that `generate-semver-lock` can produce nondeterministic `semver-lock.json` output when multiple Forge artifacts with the same semver key are compiled with different optimizer settings, specifically citing `L2ProxyAdmin` as a concrete case. A comment from deodrone at 2026-05-26T22:09:07Z also raises a related security concern about AI data exfiltration when developers use AI tools for contract debugging.

### Flaky Test Investigation: `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_CLSync`
Issue [#21041](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21041) is tracking a regression in the `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_CLSync` test family. The latest comment from pauldowman at 2026-05-26T20:21:19Z indicates that the root cause is not a test budget bug but an `op-reth` Engine API stall. Evidence from CI logs shows L2CL-b's verifier stalled at block 40, with `op-reth` emitting `Block added to canonical chain ... number=41` but `op-node` timing out on `newPayloadV3` / `forkchoiceUpdated` RPC calls for block 41. The implication is that the bug lies within the `op-reth` Engine API or the `op-node` ⇄ `op-reth` Engine handshake. The next step is to rebase a failing branch onto `develop` to include a recent fix ([#21012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/21012)) and re-run tests to see if the flake persists.

### `op-reth` Proofs-History Exex SIGBUS Crash
Issue [#20934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20934) details SIGBUS crashes and infinite retry loops in the proofs-history exex during deep FCU rewinds. The issue was reopened by einar-oplabs at 2026-05-26T09:52:51Z, noting that point 2 of the original issue still needs to be addressed. dhyaniarun1993 at 2026-05-26T09:58:16Z is currently testing a hypothesis and awaiting input from the Reth core team regarding a possible SIGBUS race during unwind/reorg flows, specifically related to `File::set_len(ftruncate)` truncating mmap pages while another thread is reading them.

### L2CM: Prevent Silent Drift in Feature Flag Definitions
Issue [#20340](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20340) addresses the silent drift between feature flag definitions and the CI matrix, which led to audit findings. maurelian at 2026-05-26T15:40:31Z made the decision to handle this by documenting all places that need updates when adding new dev or system features, with this documentation to be placed as comments in `DevFeatures.sol` and `devFeatures.go`.

### Investigate Adding an Array of Predeploys to Increase Upgrade Safety
Issue [#19260](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19260) was reopened by ajsutton at 2026-05-26T19:10:27Z because a TODO referencing it still exists in the codebase at `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/L2/L2ContractsManager.t.sol:1060`. The TODO states: `// TODO(#19260): Refactor this when we have a proper single source of truth for the predeploys.` This indicates that the underlying architectural issue of distributed implementation knowledge across multiple data structures, as detailed in a previous comment by maurelian at 2026-03-26T14:49:12Z, remains unresolved despite a point fix in PR #19464. The issue highlights a structural gap in the upgrade pipeline where there is no centralized source of truth for which implementations need to be deployed, leading to potential silent failures in future upgrades.

### `op-supernode`: Track FCU Retry-Verify Workaround
Issue [#19772](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19772) discusses the `RewindToTimestamp` function's use of a retry-verify loop after each FCU to work around an `op-reth` race condition. ajsutton at 2026-05-26T02:18:32Z commented that this workaround was accepted as a necessary measure, as the upstream PR for a proper fix was closed as stale, and there has been no significant interest in fixing Reth's engine API to apply results synchronously.
